name: Image to Video
description: Image to Video is an overview page: browse 19 animation models and example motions, then open Video Studio to animate your image.
shortDescription: Browse image-animation models and examples, then animate in Video Studio.
fullDescription: Image to Video (#/image-to-video) is a starting page, not a generator. It has an 'Animate Any Image' section with 'Animate Your Images' and '🎯 GTM Boost', four highlight cards, an 'Available Models' grid ('19 featured models out of 188 image-to-video models in Video Studio'), five 'Example Animations' with 'Try this →', and a 'Bring Images to Life' section with 'Get Started Free'. There is no image upload or Generate button here: everything opens Video Studio (#/video). An example puts its motion prompt into Video Studio's prompt box. The model you click is not selected in Video Studio (it opens on its text-to-video list, and the page passes no model), and no image is passed, so in Video Studio you add your start image, which switches it to image-to-video, then pick the model.
bestFor: Users who want ideas for animating a still image and a quick way into Video Studio.
whenToUse: You want to see image-to-video model families (Kling I2V, Veo3 I2V, Runway I2V, Seedance I2V, Hailuo I2V, Sora 2 I2V...).
You want an example motion prompt ('smooth camera pan left', 'gentle breathing animation') filled into Video Studio.
You want GTM Boost to write a marketing video prompt.
whenToUseAnother: Use Video Studio (#/video) directly: add your image as a start frame there.
Use Animate Studio (#/animate) for character animation workflows.
Use Text to Video (#/text-to-video) when you have no image.
keyFeatures: 'Animate Your Images' and 'Get Started Free' buttons that open Video Studio.
'Example Animations' with 'Try this →' that fill Video Studio's prompt box.

featureExplanations.explanation: In 'Animate Any Image', the 'Animate Your Images' button opens Video Studio (#/video).
featureExplanations.inputRequired: None here; add your image in Video Studio.

featureExplanations.explanation: The '🎯 GTM Boost' button opens the GTM Boost window ('🎯 GTM Boost · Image to Video'). You write your idea, pick an angle, audience and goal, and click the Boost button to get a conversion-focused prompt. 'Apply' closes the window and opens Video Studio with that prompt already in the prompt box.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Turn a rough marketing idea into a ready-to-use prompt before you start.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: An idea in step 1 (otherwise the window says 'Add your ... idea first.').
featureExplanations.restrictions: Without an OpenAI key the window shows 'Add your OpenAI key for AI-written results. Until then GTM Boost uses a built-in template.'

featureExplanations.explanation: Four information cards: 'Image to Video', '188 Models', 'Motion Effects' and 'Smooth Animation'. They are not buttons.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Summary of what animating an image can do.
featureExplanations.restrictions: '188 Models' is the number of image-to-video models in Video Studio; the page grid shows 19 featured ones.

featureExplanations.explanation: A grid of 19 cards ('19 featured models out of 188 image-to-video models in Video Studio'): Kling I2V (and 1.2, 1.5, 1.6, 2.0), Veo3 I2V, Runway I2V, Wan I2V, Midjourney v7 I2V, Hunyuan I2V, Seedance I2V, Pixverse I2V, Vidu Q1/Q2 Reference, Hailuo I2V, Sora 2 I2V, OVI I2V, LTX 2 I2V and Leonardoai Motion 2.0. Clicking a card opens Video Studio.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: See which animation model families exist.
featureExplanations.restrictions: No model is passed to Video Studio, so it opens on its default text-to-video model (Seedance Lite). Add your image, then pick the image-to-video model in Video Studio.

featureExplanations.explanation: Five example cards with a model badge and 'Try this →' (for example 'Animate this image with a smooth camera pan left' with Kling I2V). Clicking one opens Video Studio with that text in the prompt box.
featureExplanations.restrictions: The badge model is not selected and no image is attached; add your image in Video Studio before generating.

featureExplanations.explanation: In 'Bring Images to Life', 'Get Started Free' opens Video Studio.

howToUse: 1. Open Image to Video (#/image-to-video). 2. Click an 'Example Animations' card for a motion prompt, or 'Animate Your Images' / 'Get Started Free'. 3. In Video Studio, add your image as the start frame (the studio switches to image-to-video models). 4. Choose the model, check the prompt and click Generate in Video Studio.
howToSteps: Click an example or 'Animate Your Images'.
In Video Studio, attach your start image.
gettingStarted: Click 'Try this →' on 'Create a dynamic zoom out effect'.
In Video Studio add your picture, check the model, and Generate.
requiredInputs: None on this page; the image is added in Video Studio.

limitationDetails.impact: Video Studio opens on Seedance Lite (text-to-video).
limitationDetails.workaround: Attach your image, then choose the model in Video Studio's picker.

limitationDetails.impact: Generating right away would make a text-to-video clip.
limitationDetails.workaround: Attach your start image in Video Studio first.

troubleshooting: Video Studio opened in text-to-video with Seedance Lite: attach your image first; the studio then switches to image-to-video models.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: My image is not being animated
steps: In Video Studio, attach the image as the start frame.
Check the model button shows an image-to-video model.

commonProblems.problem: The model I clicked is not selected
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The page does not pass a model to Video Studio, which opens on its text-to-video list.
commonProblems.howToFix: Search for the model in Video Studio's picker after attaching your image.

exampleWorkflows.title: Animate a product photo
steps: Click 'Try this →' on 'Create a dynamic zoom out effect'.
In Video Studio attach the product photo.
Pick an image-to-video model and click Generate.

useCases.title: Bringing stills to life
useCases.description: Find a motion idea and open Video Studio ready to animate.
useCases.expectedOutput: Video Studio with the motion prompt filled in.

faqs.question: Can I generate directly on this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page has no prompt box, upload, ratio or Generate button. Every button and card opens Video Studio (#/video), where the actual generation happens.

faqs.question: Where do I upload my image?
faqs.answer: In Video Studio, using its image (start frame) button. This page has no upload.

glossary.Prompt: The text you write to describe the video.
glossary.Model: The AI engine that makes the clip; each one has its own durations, ratios and options.
glossary.Prefill: When this page passes a prompt or model to Video Studio so it is already filled in.
glossary.GTM Boost: A helper window that rewrites your idea as a marketing-focused video prompt.
glossary.Image-to-video: Making a video clip that starts from a still image you supply.
glossary.Start frame: The image the generated video begins from.

tips: Describe motion and camera movement, not the picture itself; the image already shows the content.
Always attach the image in Video Studio before generating.
bestPractices: Use this page for ideas; pick the model in Video Studio after the image is attached.

verification.evidence: Read ImageToVideoPage.js: all buttons navigate to 'video'; model and example clicks call storePrefillModel([], name), which stores no model and clears any old one; counts come from i2vModels.length (188). VideoStudio.js resolves prefill_model against t2vModels only (default t2vModels[0] = Seedance Lite). prefill_prompt is read into Video Studio's prompt box and cleared.
